title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). pi_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, free on loops l_0, l_1, l_inf with l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1. phi is the outer epimorphism onto pi_{0,3}/<<l_1^2, l_inf^3>>, which is isomorphic to G^+_{0,3}, the oriented triangulated cartographic group of [C]. That group is Z/2*Z/3, isomorphic to PSL_2(Z). phi is given by the explicit formulas l_0 -> sigma_inf rho, l_1 -> sigma_inf, l_inf -> rho^{-1}. G^+_{0,3} is also identified with the orbifold pi_1 of (U_{0,3}, G_3) at a point P. If G_3 is the S_3 symmetry group, that quotient is the j-line orbifold, whose pi_1 is PSL_2(Z) containing Gamma(2)/+-1 with index 6. Profinite completion gives phi^ : pi^_{0,3} ->> G^^+_{0,3}.

This page. Gamma = Gal(Qbar/Q) acts by outer automorphisms on both groups, giving two extensions of Gamma:
- (5) top row: 1 -> pi^_{0,3} -> E_{0,3} -> Gamma -> 1, the arithmetic fundamental group of P^1_Q - {0,1,inf}.
- (4) / (5) bottom row: 1 -> G^^+_{0,3} -> M_{0,3} -> Gamma -> 1. The next page reads M_{0,3} as the 'fundamental group with singularities' of the orbifold (P^1_Q - {0}, 2{1} + 3{inf}). That is the arithmetic orbifold pi_1 of the (2,3,inf) j-line, obtained from E_{0,3} by killing l_1^2 and l_inf^3.

Claim. Saying that phi^ commutes with the Gamma-actions amounts to saying that phi^ extends to a morphism of extensions (sigma): E_{0,3} -> M_{0,3}, the identity on Gamma.

Grothendieck's view. phi^ was defined by 'formules brutales', without reference to any subgroup Pi of Aut ext_loc(pi^). So this compatibility seems to him a priori a non-trivial condition on each element of Gamma, inside Aut ext(pi^_{0,3}). He wants it made explicit through the computations of [C], alongside the congruence conditions. On the next page he suspects 'toute une kyrielle' of such conditions on Gamma, to be isolated in general.

In modern terms. This is the programme of cutting out the image of Gal(Qbar/Q) in Out(F^_2) by compatibility with orbifold quotients and symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,inf}. Conditions of exactly this kind (the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations from the S_2, Z/3 and S_3 symmetries, together with compatibility with the (2,3,inf) orbifold) become Drinfeld's GT^ relations. Variants come from M_{1,1} and SL_2(Z) compatibility (Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps, among others).
errors: For genuine Galois elements the compatibility is automatic, so it is 'non-trivial' only as a condition defining a subgroup of Aut ext(pi^_{0,3}), i.e. a GT-type constraint, not as a restriction on Gamma itself. Reasoning: once the target is identified geometrically (the map P^1-{0,1,inf} -> (2,3,inf) orbifold is defined over Q, and the S_3-quotient via j is defined over Q), the action descends. Gamma sends l_i to conjugates of l_i^{chi(sigma)}, so the closed normal subgroup generated by l_1^2 and l_inf^3 is Gamma-stable. The only real content concerns whether the 'brutal' combinatorial isomorphism pi'_{0,3} = G^+_{0,3} agrees with the geometric one up to Gamma-compatible outer automorphisms. Grothendieck's phrasing ('condition non triviale sur Gamma') is therefore ambiguous rather than wrong.
In diagram (5) the middle vertical map E_{0,3} -> M_{0,3} is a quotient (surjection), as the next page states. It is not an inclusion, so the hook-like symbol read as '∩' is misleading.

The next page says M_{0,3} is the quotient of Pi^_{0,3} by <<l_1^2, l_inf^3>>. For M_{0,3} to be an extension of Gamma this must mean the quotient of E_{0,3}; the quotient of Pi^_{0,3} itself would give G^^+_{0,3}. This looks like a slip of notation.

ideas.what: Viewing the arithmetic orbifold fundamental group of the (2,3,inf) j-line as an extension of Gamma by PSL_2(Z)^, i.e. a quotient of the arithmetic pi_1 of P^1_Q - {0,1,inf} by <<l_1^2, l_inf^3>>.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic (étale) fundamental group of an orbifold / stacky curve, M_{1,1}-type extension of G_Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse) in spirit; developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Oda, Noohi (stacky pi_1)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of M_{1,1}, SL_2(Z)^ and the Teichmüller tower; La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Requiring the outer Galois action on pi^_{0,3} to be compatible with the explicit cartographic epimorphism onto PSL_2(Z)^. This yields explicit relations that elements of the Galois image must satisfy, alongside 'conditions congruentielles'.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT^ (2-cycle/3-cycle relations from S_3-symmetry and the orbifold quotient); orbifold/M_{1,1}-compatibility conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps (1997) for SL_2(Z)/M_{1,1}-type conditions
ideas.where_published: The general programme (Galois image characterized by the Teichmüller tower) is in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific compatibility condition is unsure

ideas.what: Anticipating 'a whole string' of conditions of the same nature on Gamma, to be isolated in general.
ideas.modern_name: Hierarchy of GT-type groups (GT^, GT^_1, IGT, elliptic GT, etc.)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara, Schneps, Lochak, Nakamura, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Enriquez (elliptic)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (expected description of Gal(Qbar/Q) via automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames the compatibility of the Galois outer action with the cartographic quotient F^_2 ->> (Z/2*Z/3)^ = PSL_2(Z)^, read as the orbifold pi_1 of the S_3-quotient, as a source of explicit conditions on Galois elements. He ties these to the cartographic-group computations of [C] and to congruence conditions. This is a hands-on precursor of the GT relations and of LNS-type M_{1,1} conditions, phrased via the oriented triangulated cartographic group, apparently years before Drinfeld.
missed.quote: Le fait que l'homomorphisme (3) commute à l'action de Γ_Q = Γ me semble a priori une condition non triviale sur Γ ... qu'il faudrait bien arriver à expliciter (de même que les conditions congruentielles)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck sought GT-like defining relations via cartographic/orbifold quotients, linked to congruence phenomena. Relating GT^-type relations directly to the cartographic group action on dessins, and to congruence-subgroup conditions, is still only partially explored (e.g. which GT-type groups preserve congruence or non-congruence properties of dessins).

deep.surprise_reason: The idea that compatibility with orbifold quotients and symmetries imposes GT-type conditions on Galois images is now standard (Drinfeld, Ihara, LNS). The general programme is in the Esquisse, so this is mainly a historically interesting early, concrete instance tied to cartographic groups and congruence conditions, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Group symbol: the image writes a script/fraktur G with a hat, i.e. G^^+_{0,3}, consistent with the previous page. The transcription's \mathfrak{S} should be \mathfrak{G}.
Top row of (5): the image shows \hat{\Pi}_{0,3}, a capital Pi-like symbol, consistent with the next page.
In (5) the middle vertical symbol is a downward arrow/hook, and per the next page it is the surjection Phi. It is not a set inclusion '∩'.
'[-ou plus-] contenant' is correct: 'ou plus' is struck out, and 'contenant' is written beneath it.
